post.description:
Issues an OAuth 2.0 access token for the Daftra API. The returned token is bound to the account (tenant) identified by the request subdomain.

The primary flow is the **password grant**: submit the account owner's email (or a staff member's email) as `username` together with their `password`, plus the API application's `client_id` and `client_secret`. Both account owners and staff users can authenticate through this endpoint.

On success you receive a long-lived `Bearer` access token and a `refresh_token`. Send the access token in the `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` header on subsequent API calls.

This endpoint is public and does not itself require authentication. Request bodies may be sent as `multipart/form-data` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

grant_type.description:
The OAuth 2.0 grant type. Use `password` for interactive email/password login.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| password | Authenticate with `username` + `password` (account owner or staff email). |
| refresh_token | Exchange a `refresh_token` for a new access token. |
| client_credentials | Machine-to-machine token for the application itself. |
| authorization_code | Authorization-code (redirect-based) flow. |

client_id.description: The API application's client identifier.

username.description: The account owner's email or a staff member's email. Case-insensitive. Required for the `password` grant.

password.description: The account owner or staff member's password. Required for the `password` grant.

scope.description: Optional. Space-separated list of scopes to request. Defaults to the application's default scope when omitted.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token to exchange for a new access token. Required only when `grant_type` is `refresh_token`.

expires_in.description: Number of seconds until the access token expires.

access_token.description: The signed JWT access token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on subsequent requests.

refresh_token.description: Token used to obtain a new access token via the `refresh_token` grant.

400.description: Invalid or missing request parameters, or failed user credentials (password grant).

error.description:
Machine-readable error code.

| `error` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| invalid_request | A required parameter (such as `username` or `password`) is missing or malformed. |
| invalid_grant | The supplied user credentials are incorrect. |
| invalid_scope | The requested scope is invalid or unknown. |
| unsupported_grant_type | The `grant_type` is not supported. |

hint.description: Optional additional hint about the error.

get.description:
Returns information about the current site (account) and the authenticated principal: the business/owner profile, localization (currency, number and date formats), subscription status, and a few plugin/context flags. The payload is wrapped in a `Site` object under `data`.

Some fields are conditional:
- `is_super_admin` and `staff` are returned only when the request is authenticated as a staff member (`staff_id` > 0); `staff` is that staff member's record with the password removed.
- `expensesIsMandatoryEnabled` is returned only when the request sends the header `x-app-name: EXP`.

Authenticate with an `apikey` header or a Bearer access token.

put.description:
Edit an existing **standard invoice** by id. Send via `PUT /invoices/{id}` (or `POST /invoices/{id}`) with the full invoice payload — submitted line items, payments and custom fields replace the existing ones.

The invoice **cannot be edited** (returns 400 or 404) when it: is on a different branch than it was created on; has a valid (accepted) electronic invoice; has related credit charges, installment agreements or membership/credit renewals; falls in a closed financial period (non-draft); is tied to a closed POS shift; has a received requisition; or is selected in a production plan.

Requires edit permission — all-invoices edit access, or being the invoice's own staff with edit-own access.

post.description:
Creates multiple invoices in a single request. The request body is a **JSON array**; each element has the exact same shape as the body of **Add New Invoice** (an object with an `Invoice` member plus optional `InvoiceItem`, `Payment`, etc.).

Invoices are created **one by one and the operation is not atomic** — if one element fails validation the others are still created. The response is a **JSON array** with one result object per submitted invoice, in the same order as the request. A successful element carries the new invoice `id` and number; a failed element carries an error result with a message, so you must inspect each element to confirm it succeeded.

Per-element fields and defaulting behaviour are identical to **Add New Invoice** — see that endpoint for the full field reference.

get.description:
Updates an invoice's draft status.

Use `draft_status = 0` to **issue** a draft invoice — this assigns the official sequential invoice number and posts the invoice's payment journal entries. Use `draft_status = 1` to move an issued invoice **back to draft**, which removes those payment journal entries.

Requires permission to edit or issue invoices.

|---|---|
| 0 | Issue the invoice (remove draft) |
| 1 | Set the invoice as draft |

The request is rejected with `400` when the change is not allowed — for example the invoice is already issued, it has completed payments (so it cannot be set back to draft), it has been refunded, or its date falls within a closed financial period.

post.description:
Converts a sales order (identified by the `id` path parameter) into a new invoice.

The new invoice inherits the sales order's client, currency, shipping, discounts, adjustment, and a source link back to the sales order — these are taken from the sales order and **override** any values you send. Send `InvoiceItem` to choose which lines and quantities to convert (**partial conversion** is supported); you may also pass standard invoice fields such as `date`, `store_id`, or `draft`.

If the sales order has requisitions, conversion is limited to accepted/selected requisition lines — pass `requisition_ids[]` (query) to choose them when you hold the convert permission.

On success the invoice is created and returned with the standard creation envelope (HTTP `202` with the new invoice `id`). Requires the Sales Order module to be enabled and permission to create invoices / convert sales orders. The request is rejected with `404` when the sales order is missing, already invoiced, not permitted, or has no convertible items.

post.description:
Creates multiple refund receipts in a single request. The request body is a **JSON array**; each element has the same shape as the body of **Add New Refund Receipt** (an object with an `Invoice` member — `RefundReceipt` is also accepted — plus optional `InvoiceItem`, `Payment`, etc.).

Each element must set `Invoice.subscription_id` to the **source invoice being refunded** (despite the name, this is not a subscription). That source invoice must be an issued (non-draft) standard invoice.

Refund receipts are created **one by one and the operation is not atomic** — if one element fails the others are still created. The response is a **JSON array** with one result object per submitted element, in request order:

| Outcome | Item fields |
|---|---|
| Success | `result` = `successful`, `code` = `202`, `id`, `invoice_number` |
| Failure | `message`, `validation_errors` (and sometimes `error_type` / `extra_data`) |

The overall response is `200` regardless of individual outcomes, so you must inspect each element. Per-element field and defaulting behaviour is identical to **Add New Refund Receipt** — see that endpoint for the full field reference.

Record a payment against an invoice.

Send the payment under an `InvoicePayment` object. To create several payments in one call, send an **array** of payment objects under `InvoicePayment` instead.

**Required:** `invoice_id`, `amount`, and `payment_method`. `payment_method` must be one of the account's active configured payment methods (e.g. `cash`, `bank`, `cheque`, or an enabled online gateway key).

Several fields are set automatically and cannot be supplied by the caller: the payment `status` (new payments are marked Completed), the recording staff, the currency (taken from the invoice), and the payer contact details (name/address are copied from the invoice's client). Any such fields included in the request are ignored.

On success the endpoint responds with `202 Accepted` and the new payment `id`.

| `fields[]` | Restrict the returned columns. |
| `search` | Free-text search. |

post.description:
Creates a new booking (an appointment-style record). Provide the client, the booking date, and one or more services to book.

Each entry in `InvoiceItem` must reference an **active bookable service** — a product of type *Service* that has a duration configured and belongs to at least one category. A request whose services are not valid bookable services is rejected with `Please Enter Valid Service`.

The end time is calculated automatically from the services' durations, and the booking's staff and status are assigned automatically — you do not send them. Set `Invoice.convert` to `1` to immediately convert the new booking into an invoice within the same request; the response then also returns `invoice_id`.

The `.json` extension is optional and does not change the response.

parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

date.description: Required. The booking date in `dd/mm/yyyy` format.

start_time.description: Optional. Start time in 24-hour `HH:mm` format. Defaults to the start of the day when omitted.

description.description: Optional. Free-text note stored on the booking.

branch_id.description: Optional. The branch the booking belongs to. Defaults to the request's current branch.

convert.description: Optional. Set to `1` to also convert the created booking into an invoice in the same request; the response then includes `invoice_id`. Defaults to `0`.

|---|---|

post.description:
Creates a new work order.

Requires the `Add new work orders` permission. The request body must be wrapped in a `WorkOrder` object. Only `title` is required.

Several fields are set automatically and cannot be controlled by the caller: the work order `number` is generated when omitted, `start_date` defaults to today when omitted, the creator is recorded as the authenticated user, and `status` is set to Open (or Draft when `is_draft` is sent). On success the new work order id is returned with HTTP 202.

put.description:
Updates an existing work order.

Requires permission to edit the work order (`Edit & remove all work orders`, or `Edit & remove his work orders` for one the staff created or is assigned to). The request body must be wrapped in a `WorkOrder` object; `title` and `start_date` are required.

A **Closed** work order cannot be edited and returns `400`. The same operation is also reachable via `POST /work_orders/{id}`.

delete.description:
Deletes a work order by its identifier.

Requires permission to edit/remove the work order, and the work order must have no blocking related transactions (invoices, credit notes, refunds, expenses, requisitions, purchase orders, etc.) — otherwise the request is rejected with `403`. Its start date must not fall within a closed financial period.

For API callers the deletion is confirmed automatically (no confirmation step). On success the deleted-confirmation message is returned with HTTP 200.

post.description:
Adds a single **component (raw-material) line** to an existing bundle product by creating one product-bundle record.

- `product_id` — the component product to add to the bundle.
- `bundle_product_id` — the existing bundle product the component is attached to.
- `quantity` — how many units of the component the bundle consumes.

Both `product_id` and `bundle_product_id` are required and must reference existing products.

> To build a whole bundle product **and** its lines in one request, create the product entity instead and send the lines as a nested `product_bundles` array; this endpoint adds one line at a time.

put.description:
Update an existing **Unit Template** (v2 native-entity API).

`PUT https://{subdomain}.daftra.com/v2/api/entity/unit_template/{id}`

## URL rules

- **The record id goes in the path.** `/v2/api/entity/unit_template` without an id is the
  *collection* path — it only accepts `POST` (create). A `PUT` there returns
  `405 The PUT method is not supported for route api/entity/unit_template. Supported methods: POST.`
- **No trailing slash.** A URL ending in `/` is answered with a `301` to the same URL without it,
  and HTTP clients drop the request method **and body** when they follow a `301` — the call arrives
  as a `GET` and you get a misleading "The GET method is not supported" error. Never combine
  `curl --location` with `--request PUT`.

## Authentication

`Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` from the OAuth password grant. The `apikey` header belongs to
the v1 CakePHP `/api2` API and is ignored on this surface.

## Body semantics

- **`id` in the body is what makes this an update.** Omit it and the request **inserts a new record**
  and returns the new id — the `{id}` in the URL does not prevent that. Always send `id`, matching the URL.
- Fields you omit keep their stored value (partial merge)…
- …**except `active`, which is a checkbox: omitting it stores `0`.** Send it on every update.
- `branch_id` and `staff_id` are assigned by the server (auto-branch / auto-staff) and ignored if sent.
- `created` / `modified` are read-only.

## Unit factors

- The array key is **`unit_templates_unit_factors`** (parent table + subform name). `unit_factors`
  is silently ignored — the rows are dropped without an error.
- The array **replaces the whole set**: a row **with** `id` is updated, a row **without** `id` is
  inserted, and any existing row you leave out is **deleted**.
- Omit the key entirely to leave the existing factors untouched.

## Responses

| Code | Body | When |
| ---- | ---- | ---- |
| 200 | `{message, id}` | Saved. `message` is localised to the site language — match on the status and `id`, not the text. |
| 400 | `{message}` or `{message, errors}` | `Record not found` for an unknown id, or `Entity not saved` with per-field errors. |
| 401 | `{error}` | Caller lacks the update permission for this entity. |
| 405 | `{message}` | Wrong method for the path — usually a missing id or a followed trailing-slash redirect (see *URL rules*). |

put.description:
Updates an existing journal entry and replaces its line items.

**Amounts.** Send the line amounts as `currency_debit` / `currency_credit`, in the journal's currency. The base-currency `debit` / `credit` fields are derived by the server (`currency_* x currency_rate`) and anything sent in them is overwritten - a payload that carries only `debit` / `credit` has every line discarded and is rejected with `400`.

**Line items are a full replacement.** The `JournalTransaction` array is the complete set: a line with `id` updates that line, a line without `id` is inserted, and any existing line missing from the array is deleted. A line `id` that belongs to a different journal is rejected with `400`.

**Balance.** The sum of `currency_debit` must equal the sum of `currency_credit`; `total_debit` and `total_credit` on the journal are recomputed from the lines and cannot be set directly.

The `{id}` in the URL identifies the journal. `Journal.id` in the body is optional, but when present it must match the URL id.

post.description:
Create a journal category — a folder in the chart of accounts that groups other categories and posting accounts.

This endpoint creates **categories only**. To create a posting account that journal entries can be booked to, use *Add New Journal Account* instead; an `account_type` sent in this request is ignored.

**Required:** `code` and `name`.

`code` must be **numeric**, and it must not already be used by another category **or** by a journal account — codes are shared across both. Use *GET All Journal Cats* and *GET All Journal Accounts* to find a free code; by convention a child's code extends its parent's (a child of `5` is numbered `51`, `52`, …).

> **A code that is already in use does not return an error.** The request answers with `302` and a `Location` header pointing at the chart-of-accounts page, and no JSON body — so check that the code is free before posting, and configure your client not to follow redirects for this call.

Omit `journal_cat_id` to create a top-level category, or set it to the reference of the parent category to nest this one beneath it.

Only the `JournalCat` object is read from the request body; any other top-level object is ignored. `Content-Type` must be `application/json`; another content type, or a body that is not valid JSON, returns `500`.

> **Do not send `id` when creating.** If it holds the reference of an existing category, that category is overwritten instead of a new one being created. Use the *Edit Journal Cats* endpoint to change an existing category.

Requires the *Manage Journal Accounts* permission.

On success the endpoint responds with `202 Accepted` and the reference of the new category.

post.description:
Adds a cost center. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The request body is a flat JSON object. The account layer applies **no field validation** here, so the only hard requirements are the two fields the database cannot default: `cost_center_id` and `cost_center_ids`. Omitting either fails with a `400`.

In practice you should always send `name` and `code` as well — if omitted they are silently stored as an empty name and an empty/`0` code, which is rarely useful. `code` must be **unique** across the account; a duplicate `code` fails with a `400`.

`is_primary` marks a cost center as primary (root) or secondary (child):

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Primary (root) |
| 0 | Secondary (child); defaults to `0` when omitted |

`cost_center_id` is the id of the parent cost center — send `0` for a primary/root cost center, or the parent's id for a child. `cost_center_ids` is the comma-separated ancestor path of parent ids; it **must be non-empty** (an empty string is rejected), and it is not maintained automatically, so the caller supplies it.

`branch_id`, `status`, `id`, `created` and `modified` are assigned by the server and are not settable through this endpoint.

On success the response is `{ "message": "...", "id": <new id> }`. The message is localized to the caller's language (for example `Cost center Added Successfully` in English).

The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number. Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters.

Results can be scoped to an approval tab with the `status` query parameter; when it is omitted the request is redirected so that `status=all` is applied by default.

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `status` | Approval tab to list. One of `all`, `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `pending_on_me`. Defaults to `all`. |
| `filter[<field>][<operator>]` | Filter by a field, e.g. `filter[staff_id][equal]=1`. |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`. |
| `fields[]` | Restrict the returned columns. |
| `search` | Free-text search. |

**Filterable fields.** Filter with `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`. The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | `filter[id][equal]=5` |
| `staff_id` | integer (staff) | `filter[staff_id][equal]=1` |
| `type` | enum (`leave`, `half_leave`, `delay`, `early`) | `filter[type][equal]=leave` |
| `date_from` | date | `filter[date_from][greater_than_equal]=2026-01-01` |
| `date_to` | date | `filter[date_to][less_than_equal]=2026-12-31` |
| `created` | datetime | `filter[created][greater_than_equal]=2026-01-01` |
| `approved_by` | integer (staff) | `filter[approved_by][equal]=3` |
| `shift_type` | enum (`primary`, `secondary`) | `filter[shift_type][equal]=primary` |

Filter by approval state with the `status` tab parameter (above), not `filter[status]`. In practice the endpoint accepts a filter on any existing column.

**Sortable fields.** Sort with `sort[<field>]=asc|desc`. The field intended for sorting:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `created` | datetime | `sort[created]=desc` |

When no `sort` is given, results are returned newest-first (by `id`, descending). In practice the endpoint accepts a sort on any existing field.

The response is a standard paginated envelope; each item in `data` is a leave-application record. Which staff members' applications are returned depends on the caller's leave permissions (own applications, or those they may view/approve for others).

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of branches for the account.

This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. **Requires the Branches plugin to be enabled on the account.**

The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number. `/branch/list` and `/branch/list/1` return the same result. Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters.

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>][<operator>]` | Filter rows by a field's value, e.g. `filter[status][equal]=1`. |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `sort[code]=asc`. |

**Filterable fields.** Filter with `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`. The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | `filter[code][equal]=00001` |
| `status` | integer (`1`, `2`, `3`) | `filter[status][equal]=1` |

**Sorting.** Sort with `sort[<field>]=asc|desc`, e.g. `sort[code]=asc`. No field is specifically flagged for sorting; the list will in fact filter and sort on any existing column. When no `sort` is given the default ordering is newest first (`id` descending).

This API exposes six branch fields only — `id`, `name`, `status`, `created`, `modified`, and `code`. Other branch attributes (phone numbers, address, city, state, country, assigned staff, SMTP account, map location) are **not** available through this endpoint.

The `status` value is one of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `1` | Active |
| `2` | Inactive |
| `3` | Suspended |

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Items per page. Defaults to `20`.

parameters.name: filter[<field>][<operator>]
parameters.description: Filter rows by a field's value, e.g. `filter[status][equal]=1` or `filter[code][equal]=00001`. Filterable fields intended for use: `code`, `status` (the API also accepts any other existing column).

parameters.name: sort[<field>]
parameters.description: Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `sort[code]=asc`. Default ordering is `id` descending.

post.description:
Updates an existing branch. This posts to the same `/v2/api/entity/branch` path as create; the record to update is identified by the **`id` in the request body**. If `id` is omitted a new branch is created instead.

This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. **Requires the Branches plugin to be enabled on the account.**

**This is a partial merge, not a full overwrite.** Only the fields you include in the body are changed; any field you omit is left untouched. The updatable fields are `name`, `code`, and `status`. Only these fields can be updated — `id`, `name`, `status`, `created`, `modified`, and `code`. Other branch attributes (phone numbers, address, city, state, country, assigned staff, SMTP account, map location) are **not** available through this endpoint.

On success the response is `{ "message": <localized text>, "id": <id> }`. The success message is the same text returned by create, so it does not distinguish an update from an insert.

The `status` value is one of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `1` | Active |
| `2` | Inactive |
| `3` | Suspended |

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of purchase debit notes for the account. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. It requires the **Inventory** plugin to be active.

A purchase debit note is a purchase document that shares storage with purchase orders and is identified by its document type. This endpoint returns only debit-note records.

### Data-level path segment

The trailing path segment (`-1`) is the **relation data level** — how deeply related records are eager-loaded — not a page number. Use `-1` (load base record with light relations only). Calling the list **without** a data level (`.../purchase_debit_note/list`) attempts to eager-load the full relation graph and fails with a `400` database error, so always include the segment.

### Pagination & query parameters

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>]` | Filter by a field's value, e.g. `filter[no]=PDN-0001` or `filter[supplier_id]=1`. |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `sort[date]=desc`. Default ordering is newest first (`id` descending). |
| `version` | Set to `2` to run each row through the listing formatter (adds display-formatted values); the top-level envelope is unchanged. |

**Filterable fields.** Filter with `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>` (the operator is optional; `filter[<field>]=<value>` uses a default match). The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `no` | string | `filter[no]=PDN-0001` |
| `supplier_id` | integer (supplier) | `filter[supplier_id]=1` |
| `date` | date | `filter[date][greater_than_equal]=2026-01-01` |
| `summary_total` | number | `filter[summary_total][greater_than_equal]=100` |
| `tags` | string | `filter[tags]=urgent` |

**Sortable fields.** Sort with `sort[<field>]=asc|desc`. The fields intended for sorting:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | date | `sort[date]=desc` |
| `no` | string | `sort[no]=asc` |
| `created` | datetime | `sort[created]=desc` |

The API will in fact filter and sort on any existing column of the record; the tables above list the fields the product surfaces for this entity. With no `sort`, results are ordered by `id` descending.

### Response

The response is a standard paginated envelope (`current_page`, `data`, `per_page`, `total`, `last_page`, and the page-URL/link fields). Each item in `data` is a flat purchase debit note record.

`payment_status` and `requisition_delivery_status` are returned as codes; their meanings are listed on those fields below.

post.description:
Creates a purchase debit note. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. It requires the **Inventory** plugin to be active.

A purchase debit note shares storage with purchase orders and is identified by its document type, so **`type` must be `14`** — sending a different type (or omitting it) fails with a `400` (`"error": "Record Not Found"`) because the entity can only be resolved for type `14`.

### Request body

The body is a flat JSON object. The account layer enforces exactly three required fields — omitting any of them returns `422`:

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `supplier_business_name` | Required, non-empty. |
| `draft` | Required. `1` = save as draft, `0` = finalized. |
| `summary_total.currency` | Required, non-empty (the currency of the totals object). |

In addition, `type` must be `14` for the record to save (enforced below the validation layer with a `400`).

All other fields are optional. `no` (the debit-note number) is generated automatically when omitted. `currency_code` and `supplier_id` are optional. Server-managed fields (`id`, `created`, `modified`, `branch_id`, `site_id`, `staff_id`, payment/summary totals) are assigned by the server.

### Line items

Line items are sent under the **`purchase_debit_notes_items`** array (each entry becomes a purchase-order-item row). Each item takes `product_id`, `item` (name), `description`, `unit_price`, `quantity`, `discount`, `discount_type`, `tax1`, `tax2`, and optional `col_3`..`col_5` extra columns.

### Statuses

`requisition_delivery_status`:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Received |
| 2 | Rejected |
| 3 | Pending |
| 4 | Partially Received |
| 5 | Partially Rejected |

On success the response is `{ "message": "...", "id": <new id> }`; the message is localized to the caller's language.

### Ordering
Newest first — `id` descending — unless you pass a `sort` parameter.

### Branch scoping
When the Branches add-on is enabled, results are automatically limited to your current branch. To widen the scope:

| Goal | How |
|---|---|
| A specific branch | `request_branch_id=<branch id>` |
| Every branch you have access to | `filter[branch_id][equal]=-1` |

Packages stored without a branch are not returned while branch scoping is in effect.

### Deleted packages
Deleted packages are excluded, so `deleted_at` is always `null` in this response. Fetch a deleted package directly by its id if you need it.

### Filtering
Use `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`. Omitting the operator means `equal` — `filter[status]=1` is the same as `filter[status][equal]=1`.

| Operator | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `equal` | equals (default) |
| `not_equal` | not equal |
| `in` / `not_in` | in / not in a list of values |
| `like` | partial text match |
| `gt` / `gte` / `from` | greater than / greater than or equal |
| `lt` / `lte` / `to` | less than / less than or equal |
| `is_null` / `is_not_null` | value is / is not empty |

Fields intended for filtering: `name`, `price`, `period_value`, `status`, `product_id`. Filtering on an unrecognised field returns `400`.

### Sorting
Use `sort[<field>]=asc` or `sort[<field>]=desc`, e.g. `sort[name]=asc`.

- The trailing `1` in the path is an optional data-detail level. It has no effect for packages, which are always returned as flat records.

A body **without** `id` creates a new package instead of updating one, and still replies with an "Added Successfully" message. Always send `id`.

### Only the fields you send are changed — with two exceptions
Fields you leave out keep their current values. The exceptions are the two reference fields:

| Field | Left out of the body |
|---|---|
| `branch_id` | **Set to `null`** — the package loses its branch and stops appearing in *Get All Packages* |
| `product_id` | **Set to `null`** — the package is unlinked from its product |

So resend `branch_id` and `product_id` on every update, even when they are not changing.

### Clearing a text value
Sending `null` for `name`, `description`, `price`, `period_value`, `period_unit`, `status` or `type` leaves the current value untouched. Send an empty string (`""`) to clear a text field.

### Send `Accept: application/json`
This endpoint answers with a redirect to a web page instead of JSON when the request does not ask for JSON. Always send `Accept: application/json`.

### Other notes
- A successful update replies `Package Added Successfully` — the same wording as a create. Do not read it as proof that a new package was inserted; check the `id` you sent.
- An `id` that does not exist returns `400` with `"error": "Record Not Found"`, not `404`.
- Body keys that are not package fields are ignored silently — a misspelled field name is not reported as an error.
- `modified` is refreshed automatically; `created` and `deleted_at` should be omitted.
- Values are not validated against the lists below before they reach the database, so an out-of-range value fails as a save error rather than a field-level validation error.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of records for a workflow-type entity. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

Workflow-type entities are configurable record types (for example maintenance orders or service requests). The `workflow_id` path segment selects the workflow type, and the resource prefix plus that id form the entity key `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}`. Each record is a work-order-based row belonging to that type. The available fields — including any custom fields — are defined by the selected workflow type's configuration, so the record shape varies between workflow types; custom fields are returned under the `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}_custom_data` object.

The trailing path segment is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number or a response-format extension. Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters; results can be narrowed with `filter[...]`, ordered with `sort[...]`, and trimmed with `fields`.

Filter and sort act on the record's **own columns**. The fields below are an example for a maintenance-order workflow — the exact set is workflow-specific. Custom-data fields (returned under `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}_custom_data`) are **not** filterable or sortable through this endpoint.

**Filterable fields (example).** `filter[<field>]=<value>` (exact) or `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `number` | string | `filter[number][like]=000` |
| `title` | string | `filter[title][like]=order` |
| `start_date` | date | `filter[start_date][greater_than_equal]=2026-01-01` |
| `client_id` | integer | `filter[client_id][equal]=5` |

(`filter[status]` is currently ineffective for this entity, and a `search` query parameter has no effect — use `filter[...]`.)

**Sorting.** Sort with `sort[<field>]=asc|desc` (e.g. `sort[number]=desc`) on the record's columns. The scalar `sort=field` / `sort=-field` form is not supported (HTTP 400), and no default order is guaranteed — always pass `sort[...]` for stable ordering.

parameters.name: workflow_id
parameters.description: The id of the workflow type whose records to list. Combined with the resource prefix this forms the entity key `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of records per page. Defaults to `20`.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Filter on the record's own columns, as `filter[<field>]=<value>` (exact) or `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>` (e.g. `filter[number][like]=000`). Only records matching all filters are returned. Custom-data fields are **not** filterable through this endpoint (see the endpoint description).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort by a field using the bracket form `sort[<field>]=asc|desc` (e.g. `sort[number]=desc`). The scalar form `sort=field` / `sort=-field` is not supported and returns HTTP 400. No default ordering is guaranteed — pass `sort[...]` for a stable order.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of fields to include in each returned record.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Set to `2` to return each record through the display formatter — notably file/media fields (e.g. staff photos) come back as fully-qualified URLs. The response keys are otherwise unchanged.

Creates a record in a workflow-type entity. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The `workflow_id` path segment selects the workflow type (entity key `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}`); the new record is a work-order-based row stamped with that type. The request body is a **flat object** whose keys are the workflow type's fields. The standard fields are listed below; custom fields for the workflow type are supplied under the `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}_custom_data` object.

**Required fields are defined by the selected workflow type** and enforced server-side; when a required field is missing the response is `422` with an `errors` map naming each field. For example, workflow type 1 (Maintenance Orders) requires `number.code`, `start_date`, and `budget.currency`. The record number itself is assigned by the server (submit only `number.code`).

On success the `message` is localized to the workflow type's name, e.g. `"<name> Added Successfully"`.

put.description:
Updates a record in a workflow-type entity. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. Both `PUT` and `POST` to this path are accepted.

The `workflow_id` path segment selects the workflow type (entity key `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}`) and `record_id` identifies the record. The request body is a **flat object** whose keys are the workflow type's fields and **must include `id` matching `record_id`**. Custom fields are supplied under the `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}_custom_data` object (include its existing row `id` to update in place).

**Required fields are defined by the selected workflow type** and enforced server-side; a missing required field returns `400` with an `errors` map (note: unlike create, which returns `422`). On success the `message` is localized to the workflow type's name, e.g. `"<name> Updated Successfully"`.

404.description: The record could not be loaded for update.

post.description:
Fetches data for **multiple entities in a single request**. The request body is a JSON **array** of sub-requests; each sub-request independently reads one entity — either a single record (`show`) or a filtered list (`list`).

`POST /v2/api/multi-entity`

The response is a **single JSON object** whose keys are each sub-request's `alias` (or its `key` when no alias is given). Each value holds that sub-request's result, so one call can return, for example, an invoice together with its related requisitions.

## Sub-request fields

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| key | Yes | The entity key to read (e.g. `invoice`, `requisition`, `follow_up_reminder`). |
| action | Yes | `show` to fetch a single record, `list` to fetch a filtered list. Any other value returns `{ "error": "Action not found" }` under that alias. |
| options | Yes | Depends on `action`. For `show`: the record **id**. For `list`: a **filters object** (see below). |
| alias | No | The key under which this sub-request's result appears in the response. Defaults to `key`. Use it to disambiguate two sub-requests that read the same entity. |
| level | No | Data-detail level — how deeply related records are loaded. Defaults to `1`. Higher levels return more nested relations. |

### `options` by action

- **`show`** — `options` is the record id, e.g. `"options": "172185"`.
- **`list`** — `options` is an object of filter conditions merged into the listing query, e.g. `"options": { "order_id": "172185", "order_type": 3 }`. Any field the target entity supports may be used.

## Response

Always returns **HTTP 200**. The body is an object keyed by each sub-request's `alias`:

- A `show` sub-request → the record object (with a `custom_data` property holding the record's custom-field values, when the entity has any).
- A `list` sub-request → a paginated envelope (`data` array plus `current_page`, `per_page`, `total`, `last_page`, and page-URL fields).
- A failed sub-request → `{ "error": "<message>" }`.

Sub-requests are processed independently: a failure in one (unknown action, inactive plugin, no permission to view the record, or an otherwise invalid sub-request) is reported as an `error` object under that alias and never fails the whole call. The overall HTTP status is always `200`.

> **Permissions:** a `show` sub-request requires permission to view the requested entity; without it that alias returns `{ "error": "You are not allowed to view this page" }`.

## Authentication

Send an OAuth Bearer access token in the `Authorization` header. Also send `Accept: application/json`.

get.description:
Generic, metadata-driven listing endpoint for the v2 API. It returns a **paginated, filtered, sorted** list of records for any supported entity, using a single consistent query grammar.

`GET /v2/api/entity/{entity}/list/{level}`

- **`{entity}`** — the entity key to list (e.g. `invoice`, `client`, `product`). The endpoint works for every listable entity; the enum on the `entity` path parameter is a representative sample, not the complete set.
- **`{level}`** — the *data-detail level*: how deeply related records are loaded. It is **not** a page number. Higher levels return more nested relations.

  | Level | What is returned |
  |---|---|
  | -1 | Base record fields only, no related records |
  | 0 | Own fields + one-to-one related records |
  | 1 | Own fields + one-to-one + belongs-to + one-to-many (one level deep) |
  | 2 | Same as level 1 plus one extra level of nested relations (default) |
  | 3 | Even deeper nesting |

## Pagination

Paging is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters, **not** by the URL. The response is a standard paginated envelope (`data` array + `current_page`, `per_page`, `total`, `last_page`, page-URL fields).

## Filtering

Filters use bracket syntax: `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`. Combine conditions with `filter[and][...]` and `filter[or][...]` groups. See the `filter[<field>][<operator>]` parameter for the full list of operators.

## Sorting

Sort with `sort[<field>]=<direction>`, where direction is `asc` or `desc`. Multiple sort keys are applied in order, e.g. `sort[created]=desc&sort[id]=asc`.

## Field selection

Restrict the returned columns with `fields[]=<column>` (repeat for each column). When omitted, all fields for the requested level are returned.

## Authentication

Send an OAuth Bearer access token in the `Authorization` header.

parameters.name: entity
parameters.description: The entity key to list. The listed values are a representative sample — the endpoint supports every listable entity (core and custom).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description:
Response shape / listing mode. Defaults to `api` when omitted.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| api | Paginated API response (default). Rows are reshaped so related records are nested objects. |
| listing | Paginated response used by the web UI listing (v2 formatting). |
| count | Returns only the total count of matching records. |
| export | Returns data prepared for export. |
| nav | Navigation mode; used with `current_id` to fetch neighbouring records. |

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to return. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of records per page. Defaults to `20`.

parameters.name: fields[]
parameters.description: Restrict the returned columns. Repeat for each column, e.g. `fields[]=id&fields[]=no`. When omitted, all fields for the requested level are returned.

parameters.name: sort[<field>]
parameters.description: Sort the results. Use `sort[<field>]=<direction>` where direction is `asc` or `desc`. Repeat for multiple keys; they are applied in the given order, e.g. `sort[created]=desc&sort[id]=asc`. When omitted, a saved sorting preference or the primary key is used.

parameters.name: filter[<field>][<operator>]
parameters.description:
Filter the results. Repeat the parameter for each condition.

**Syntax:** `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>` (omitting the operator is equivalent to `equal`).

**Operators**

| Operator | Meaning |
|---|---|
| equal | Equals (`=`) — the default when no operator is given |
| not_equal | Not equal (`!=`) |
| gt | Greater than (`>`) |
| lt | Less than (`<`) |
| gte / from | Greater than or equal (`>=`) |
| lte / to | Less than or equal (`<=`) |
| like | Contains (`LIKE %value%`) |
| in | In a list of values |
| not_in | Not in a list of values |
| is_null | Field is null |
| is_not_null | Field is not null |

Only the operators above are recognized; any other keyword is treated as `equal`. Express a range with two conditions (`filter[amount][from]=10&filter[amount][to]=99`); there is no `between` operator.

**AND / OR groups**

Wrap conditions in `filter[and][...]` or `filter[or][...]` to group them. The OR group is the usual way to run a keyword search across several fields, e.g. `filter[or][no][like]=INV&filter[or][client_business_name][like]=INV`.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Set to `2` to return records formatted with the v2 field formatters.

parameters.name: image_size
parameters.description: Requested image size for record images. Only applies when `version=2`.

parameters.name: request_branch_id
parameters.description: Scope the results to a specific branch by its ID.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: Response language. Accepts `ar` or `en`. The `Accept-Language` header is also honoured.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

data.description: The matching records. Each row carries the entity's own fields at the top level plus nested objects for its related records (depth depends on `{level}`). The exact fields depend on the requested entity.

from.description: Index of the first record on this page (null when empty).

next_page_url.description: URL of the next page (null on the last page).

prev_page_url.description: URL of the previous page (null on the first page).

to.description: Index of the last record on this page (null when empty).

400.description: The entity does not exist, its plugin is not active, or the entity is not listable. Example messages: `Entity Not exists`, `Plugin not active`.

error.description: Human-readable error message.

401.description: The access token is missing/invalid, or the account lacks permission to view this entity. Example message: `You are not allowed to view this page`.

error.description: Human-readable error message.

get.description:
Activates or deactivates a marketplace app for the current site.

Send `true` in the `status` path segment to activate the app, or any other value to deactivate it. When the app is not yet installed for the site, it is first installed in a deactivated state and then the requested action is applied.

The response body carries a numeric `code` describing the outcome:

| `code` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Error — app not found |
| 1 | App activated |
| 2 | Settings required — the app must be configured before it can be activated |
| 3 | App deactivated |
| 4 | Payment required — the app has not been purchased or renewed |

Successful activation/deactivation and the not-found case return HTTP `200`; the *settings required* (`2`) and *payment required* (`4`) cases return HTTP `400`. Branch on `status`/`code`, not only on the HTTP status.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The marketplace app id (the `id` of the app in the apps catalogue) to activate or deactivate.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Whether to activate or deactivate the app. Send `true` to activate; any other value deactivates.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

200.description:
Activation/deactivation outcome. Example bodies:

Activated:
```json
{ "status": true, "code": 1, "msg": "App activated successfully" }
```
Deactivated:
```json
{ "status": true, "code": 3, "msg": "App deactivated successfully" }
```
App not found (still HTTP 200):
```json
{ "status": false, "code": 0, "msg": "App not found" }
```

schema.description: The activation/deactivation outcome. Successful activation, successful deactivation, and the not-found case all return HTTP `200` — inspect `status`/`code` to distinguish them.

status.description: `true` when the requested activation or deactivation succeeded; `false` when the app id was not found.

code.description:
Outcome code. For HTTP `200` responses this is one of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | App activated |
| 3 | App deactivated |
| 0 | App not found |

msg.description: Localized, human-readable outcome message (e.g. `App activated successfully`, `App deactivated successfully`, `App not found`).

400.description:
Activation blocked. Example bodies:

Settings required:
```json
{ "status": false, "code": 2, "msg": "Settings Required" }
```
Payment required:
```json
{ "status": false, "code": 4, "msg": "You cannot activate this application because it has not been purchased or renewed. Please complete the purchase first." }
```

schema.description: The app cannot be activated yet. Returned when the app still requires configuration, or has not been purchased/renewed.

status.description: Always `false` for this response.

code.description:
Reason code:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 2 | Settings required — the app must be configured before it can be activated |
| 4 | Payment required — the app has not been purchased or renewed |

401.description: Authentication failed. Either `{ "message": "Unauthenticated." }` (no/invalid credentials) or `{ "error": "Not authorized." }` (API key lacks access to this endpoint).

schema.description: Authentication failed or was missing.

message.description: Returned when no valid token/API key is supplied.

error.description: Returned when an API key is valid but not authorized for this endpoint.
error.example: Not authorized.

get.description:
Locks or unlocks an entity record on behalf of an installed app.

Intended for third-party app integrations: an installed app can lock a specific record of any entity it has access to (preventing further edits) or unlock it again. Send `true` in the `lock` path segment to lock the record; any other value unlocks it.

Authenticated with an OAuth bearer token. The response is always HTTP `200` with a `{ status, msg }` object — inspect `status` to tell success from the two failure cases (the app is not installed/active for the site, or the record was not found).

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: The installed app's id (the app performing the lock/unlock).

parameters.name: entityKey
parameters.description: The entity key of the record to lock/unlock (e.g. `product`, `invoice`).

parameters.name: entityId
parameters.description: The id of the record within the entity.

parameters.name: lock
parameters.description: Send `true` to lock the record; any other value unlocks it.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

200.description:
Lock/unlock outcome. Example bodies:

Locked:
```json
{ "status": true, "msg": "Record locked successfully" }
```
Unlocked:
```json
{ "status": true, "msg": "Record unlocked successfully" }
```
App not installed/inactive (still HTTP 200):
```json
{ "status": false, "msg": "App is not installed or inactive" }
```
Record not found (still HTTP 200):
```json
{ "status": false, "msg": "Record not found" }
```

schema.description: The lock/unlock outcome. Always returned with HTTP `200` — inspect `status` to distinguish success from the two failure cases.

status.description: `true` when the record was locked/unlocked; `false` when the app is not installed/active for the site, or the record was not found.

msg.description:
Localized, human-readable outcome message.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Record locked successfully | The record is now locked. |
| Record unlocked successfully | The record is now unlocked. |
| App is not installed or inactive | The app is not installed or not active for the current site. |
| Record not found | No record matches the given entity/id. |

schema.description: Authentication failed or was missing (a valid OAuth bearer token is required).

message.description: Returned when no valid access token is supplied.

get.description:
Returns the activation status of a marketplace app for the current site.

An app is reported active only when it is **installed and active** for the authenticated site. The response is always HTTP `200` with a `{ status, msg }` object — including when the app id does not exist, in which case `status` is `false` and `msg` is `App not found`. Use the `status` boolean (not the HTTP code) to branch.

| `status` | `msg` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `true` | App is active | The app is installed and active for the current site. |
| `false` | App is deactivated | The app exists but is not active for the current site. |
| `false` | App not found | No app matches the given id (or the app is unavailable). |

The `msg` text is localized to the account language.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The marketplace app id (the `id` of the app in the apps catalogue) whose activation status you want to check.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

200.description:
Activation status of the app for the current site. Example bodies:

Active:
```json
{ "status": true, "msg": "App is active" }
```
Deactivated:
```json
{ "status": false, "msg": "App is deactivated" }
```
Not found (still HTTP 200):
```json
{ "status": false, "msg": "App not found" }
```

schema.description: The activation status. Always returned with HTTP `200`, including for a not-found app — inspect `status`/`msg` to distinguish the outcomes.

status.description: `true` only when the app is installed and active for the current site; `false` when it is deactivated, or when no app matches the id.

msg.description:
Human-readable, localized status message.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| App is active | Installed and active for the current site. |
| App is deactivated | Exists but not active for the current site. |
| App not found | No app matches the id (or the app is unavailable). |
